answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut in component spend this year, but the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle. Given that switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year (memory_c2) and onboarding was quick with accurate invoicing, switching primary vendor is the most direct path to achieving the mandated cost reduction. Attempting to renegotiate (memory_c4) is not viable since the incumbent has already refused to reopen price. I want to verify c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's cost-reduction magnitude and reliable onboarding history before committing to a switch, and c4 to confirm whether a different negotiation approach with the incumbent might still yield savings despite their stated refusal. Note: switching primary supply does increase delivery risk somewhat, but the primary objective is to minimize total cost of ownership without materially increasing delivery risk — a tested, previously-successful low-cost vendor mitigates this concern.
